units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Certainly. Let me.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Rings the bell .
Thanks! I don’t know what to do, Arthur, I don’t know what to do, and you are my only friend. But what a friend you are—the one friend I can trust. I can trust you absolutely, can’t I?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Enter PHIPPS.
My dear Robert, of course. Oh!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: To PHIPPS.
Bring some hock and seltzer.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: And Phipps!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Will you excuse me for a moment, Robert? I want to give some directions to my servant.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Certainly.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: When that lady calls, tell her that I am not expected home this evening. Tell her that I have been suddenly called out of town. You understand?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: The lady is in that room, my lord. You told me to show her into that room, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: You did perfectly right.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Exit PHIPPS.
What a mess I am in. No; I think I shall get through it. I’ll give her a lecture through the door. Awkward thing to manage, though.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Arthur, tell me what I should do. My life seems to have crumbled about me. I am a ship without a rudder in a night without a star.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Robert, you love your wife, don’t you?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I love her more than anything in the world. I used to think ambition the great thing. It is not. Love is the great thing in the world. There is nothing but love, and I love her. But I am defamed in her eyes. I am ignoble in her eyes. There is a wide gulf between us now. She has found me out, Arthur, she has found me out.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Has she never in her life done some folly—some indiscretion—that she should not forgive your sin?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: My wife! Never! She does not know what weakness or temptation is. I am of clay like other men. She stands apart as good women do—pitiless in her perfection—cold and stern and without mercy. But I love her, Arthur. We are childless, and I have no one else to love, no one else to love me. Perhaps if God had sent us children she might have been kinder to me. But God has given us a lonely house. And she has cut my heart in two. Don’t let us talk of it. I was brutal to her this evening. But I suppose when sinners talk to saints they are brutal always. I said to her things that were hideously true, on my side, from my stand-point, from the standpoint of men. But don’t let us talk of that.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Your wife will forgive you. Perhaps at this moment she is forgiving you. She loves you, Robert. Why should she not forgive?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: God grant it! God grant it!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Buries his face in his hands .
But there is something more I have to tell you, Arthur.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Enter PHIPPS with drinks .
Hands hock and seltzer to SIR ROBERT CHILTERN.
Hock and seltzer, sir.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Is your carriage here, Robert?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: No; I walked from the club.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Sir Robert will take my cab, Phipps.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Exit .
Robert, you don’t mind my sending you away?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Arthur, you must let me stay for five minutes. I have made up my mind what I am going to do to-night in the House. The debate on the Argentine Canal is to begin at eleven.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: A chair falls in the drawing-room .
What is that?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Nothing.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I heard a chair fall in the next room. Some one has been listening.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: No, no; there is no one there.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: There is some one. There are lights in the room, and the door is ajar. Some one has been listening to every secret of my life. Arthur, what does this mean?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Robert, you are excited, unnerved. I tell you there is no one in that room. Sit down, Robert.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Do you give me your word that there is no one there?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN
